extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and quality/format criteria for submitting computer program listings, large tables, microfiche/CD appendices, biosequence files, and Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) in U.S. patent applications, including timing, content, and technical format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: CD-ROM/CD-R format compliance (ISO 9660 and ASCII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Files submitted on compact disc must comply with ISO 9660 standard and ASCII format as required by 37 CFR 1.52(e)(3). No new matter may be introduced in presenting the file in ISO 9660 and ASCII format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ISO 9660 and ASCII; do not add new matter when converting/presenting files in required format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc contains viruses
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitted compact disc contains at least one virus, the amendment/file is objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction is required; use form paragraph 6.72.04 to object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement compact disc must include all files (amended and unamended)
rubrics_metrics.description: A replacement compact disc submitted as an amendment must include all of the files (both amended and unamended) that were on the original CD-ROM/CD-R because amendments to a compact disc can only be made by providing a replacement disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph when replacement disc fails to include all original files not cancelled by amendment; ensure full, complete replacement disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of computer program listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing is a printout that lists in appropriate sequence the instructions, routines, and other contents of a program for a computer; may be in machine or machine-independent (object or source) language that will cause a computer to perform a desired task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide general descriptions of operation and content in the specification; listing may appear directly or as a compact-disc appendix and be incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method based on listing length (≤300 lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing contained in 300 lines or fewer (with each line ≤72 characters) may be submitted either as drawings or as part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted as drawings, comply with § 1.84 and include at least one figure numeral on each sheet. If submitted as part of the specification, comply with § 1.52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning and print requirements for listings >60 lines and ≤300 lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Any listing having more than 60 lines that is submitted as part of the specification must be positioned at the end of the description but before the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to such listings must be made by substitute sheet. Alternatively, applicant may cancel and move the listing to a compact disc. If retained on paper as printouts, use direct printouts with dark solid black letters not less than 0.21 cm high, on white, unshaded, unlined paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing appendix on compact disc required for >300 lines
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing of more than 300 lines (up to 72 characters per line) must be submitted as ASCII files on compact disc as a 'computer program listing appendix' in compliance with 37 CFR 1.96(c) and must be referenced in the specification (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix will not be part of the printed patent; include an appropriate reference in the specification at the beginning of the specification immediately following any cross-reference to related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc technical specifications for program listings
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'computer program listing appendix' must be submitted on a compact disc that complies with § 1.52(e) and the following specifications: computer compatibility, operating system compatibility, line terminator, control codes, and uncompressed data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified examples: Computer Compatibility (IBM PC/XT/AT or compatibles, or Apple Macintosh); OS Compatibility (MS-DOS, MS-Windows, Unix, or Macintosh); Line Terminator (ASCII Carriage Return + ASCII Line Feed); Control Codes (must not depend on non-ASCII control characters); Compression (uncompressed data). No other formats allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple program listings and discs per application
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple computer program listings for a single application may be placed on a single compact disc; multiple compact discs may be submitted for a single application if necessary. A separate compact disc is required for each application containing a program listing appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure discs are organized per-application and that the specification references total listing files contained on all compact discs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and handling of computer program listing appendix in the file
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing appendix on compact disc will be identified on the front page of the patent but will not be part of the printed patent; the file wrapper will bear a label denoting the appendix and a special envelope will house the discs in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a statement at the beginning of the specification indicating that a computer program listing appendix on compact disc is included in the application; follow IFW processing guidance when handling discs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary microfiche practice and microfiche requirements (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microfiche appendix practice continued until March 1, 2001 for listings prepared as microfiche; such microfiche had specific requirements (first generation negative, clear header area for application number, reduction ratio, test target, title frame, consecutive numbering, pagination direction, resolution, index placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice was temporary to accommodate applicants who prepared microfiche; microfiche had to conform to former 37 CFR 1.96(c) and micrographics standards (36 CFR Part 1230).

rubrics_metrics.name: Microfiche appendix unacceptable after March 1, 2001 or if noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'microfiche appendix' filed after March 1, 2001 or a microfiche not in compliance with former 37 CFR 1.96(c) is unacceptable; a computer program listing conforming to 37 CFR 1.96 is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.64.04 to notify applicant; insert date of filing in bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables submitted in electronic form must maintain spatial relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables submitted in electronic form (§§ 1.96(c) and 1.821(c)) must maintain the spatial relationships (alignment of columns and rows) of table elements when displayed so as to visually preserve relational information. Chemical and mathematical formulae must be encoded to maintain proper positioning of characters when displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encoding/formatting must preserve intended meaning and visual layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Files on CD for tables: ASCII-only and no proprietary formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Files stored on the compact disc containing tables must contain only ASCII characters. No special formatting characters or proprietary file formats are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care so that spatial arrangement in rows and columns is maintained when opened at the Office (viewable with virtually any text viewer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper vs. CD submission thresholds for tables (≤50 pages vs ≥51 or total >100)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single table contained on 50 pages or less must be submitted either as drawings or as part of the specification in paper. A single table of 51 pages or more, or if multiple tables total more than 100 pages, the tables may be submitted on CD-ROM or CD-R in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e) and 1.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A table page is defined per 37 CFR 1.52(e)(1)(iii) as a page printed on paper in conformity with 1.52(b) and 1.58(c). Avoid artificial subdivision to evade CD submission unless subdivided files would lose relationship to the overall table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid subdividing large table to evade CD submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting a subheading to divide a large table into smaller sections of less than 51 pages should not be used to prevent submission of the table on a compact disc unless the subdivided tables are presented as numerous files on the compact disc so as to lose their relationship to the overall large table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will look at whether subdivision preserves the table's relational integrity; do not fragment to avoid electronic submission thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify landscape orientation for table files
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables in landscape orientation should be identified as landscape orientation in the transmittal letter accompanying the compact disc to allow the Office to properly upload the tables into the Image File Wrapper or other systems (37 CFR 1.52(e)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not identified, filings will be rendered as portrait mode tables by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthy tables publication policy (>200 pages or large numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: If tables on more than two hundred consecutive pages, or large numbers of tables, are submitted on CD as provided in 37 CFR 1.52(e), these lengthy tables will not be published as part of the patent document; they will be published separately on the USPTO sequence homepage as an XML file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When published separately, a standardized 'Lengthy Table' statement will be inserted in the patent document referencing the electronic copy and access instructions; examples of insertable page-wide texts are provided for application publications, patents, and SIRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CD-ROM/CD-R Requirements (Table Listing in Specification) — table too small for CD
rubrics_metrics.description: If the description contains a table of less than fifty-one (51) pages only on a CD-ROM or CD-R, this is improper: only tables of at least 51 pages may be submitted on CD-ROM or CD-R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must cancel the CD-ROM/CD-R table references in the specification, file a paper version of the table in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52, and change all references accordingly (form paragraph 6.63.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table column/row relationship must be maintained on CD
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables presented on CD-ROM/CD-R must maintain the spatial orientation of cell entries; if the data does not maintain proper row/column alignment (data misaligned), applicant must submit a replacement compact disc with the table data properly aligned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.63.02 where the area that does not maintain the alignment is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosequence filing on compact disc permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of biosequence information on compact disc is permitted in lieu of filing on paper (see MPEP §§ 2420 and 2422.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the biosequence-specific filing rules referenced in those sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS timing windows for consideration (37 CFR 1.97(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement (IDS) will be considered by the Office if filed by the applicant within one of the following: (1) within three months of the filing date of a national application (other than a CPA under §1.53(d)); (2) within three months of entry of the national stage in an international application; (3) before mailing of a first Office action on the merits; or (4) before mailing of a first Office action after filing a request for continued examination (§1.114).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary timely windows; use form procedures to ensure consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS late filing conditional acceptance (before final action/allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after the periods in paragraph (b) will be considered if filed before the mailing date of any final action under §1.113, a notice of allowance under §1.311, or any action that otherwise closes prosecution, provided it is accompanied by either the statement specified in paragraph (e) or the fee set forth in §1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required statements or fees accompany later-filed IDSs to obtain consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filing on or before issue fee (latest allowable) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed on or before payment of the issue fee may be considered if accompanied by the statement specified in paragraph (e) and the fee set forth in §1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the latest practical time to file an IDS that can be considered; include both statement and fee as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statement content for late IDS filings (37 CFR 1.97(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement under this section must state either: (1) that each item in the IDS was first cited in any communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the IDS; or (2) that no item was cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application, and, to the knowledge of the person signing after reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in §1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct option and ensure the signatory has made reasonable inquiry as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time for filing IDS under §1.136 (with possible exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: No extensions of time for filing an IDS are permitted under §1.136. However, if a bona fide attempt is made to comply with §1.98 but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File timely; if omission occurs despite bona fide attempt, petition/communication may secure limited additional time.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS is not a representation of search or materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement filed in accordance with this section shall not be construed as a representation that a search has been made or as an admission that the information cited is material to patentability as defined in §1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an IDS does not substitute for compliance with duty of disclosure; it provides a mechanism for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliant IDS placement and non-consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDS does not comply with §1.97 or §1.98, it will be placed in the file but will not be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full compliance with the content and form requirements to have the IDS considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS content requirements — list and page elements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDS must include a list of all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted for consideration. U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications must be listed in a section separately from other documents. Each page of the list must include the application number, a column for the examiner's initials next to each document, and a heading indicating that the list is an information disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow precise list formatting to facilitate examiner processing and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS required documentary attachments (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS must include a legible copy of: each foreign patent; each publication or the portion causing it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required); for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawing or the portion that caused it to be listed; and all other information or portions that caused the listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the specific portions that caused the citation to be listed to assist examiner review.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS explanation and translations for non-English documents (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each listed document not in English, a concise explanation of the relevance (as presently understood by the person designated in §1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the information) must be provided, either separate or incorporated in the specification. A copy of the translation should be provided if an English translation is in possession, custody, control, or readily available to the designated person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a knowledgeable individual prepares the concise explanation; provide translations when available to expedite examiner understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification details required for listed items (37 CFR 1.98(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. patent must be identified by inventor, patent number, and issue date. Each U.S. patent application publication must be identified by applicant, publication number, and publication date. Each U.S. application must be identified by inventor, application number, and filing date. Each foreign patent or published foreign application must be identified by country/patent office, appropriate document number, and publication date. Each publication must be identified by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, date, and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete bibliographic/identifying information for every listed item per category to meet content rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative disclosures may be treated by single copy (37 CFR 1.98(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed are substantively cumulative, a copy of one of the patents or publications may be submitted without copies of the others, provided it is stated that the other patents or publications are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly which items are cumulative to avoid unnecessary duplication of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required even if previously submitted unless earlier application relied on (37 CFR 1.98(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any cited patent, publication, pending U.S. application or other information listed in an IDS is required to be provided even if previously submitted to the Office, unless the earlier application is properly identified in the IDS and is relied on for an earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120 and the IDS in the earlier application complies with §§1.98(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify earlier applications when relying on previously-submitted materials to avoid re-submission where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSs not permitted in provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Information Disclosure Statements are not permitted in provisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b); any such statement filed in a provisional will be returned or destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file IDS in provisional applications; use other mechanisms when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure and third-party submission limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: In nonprovisional applications, applicants and those substantively involved have a duty to submit information material to patentability as defined in §1.56; 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 provide a mechanism for compliance. Third parties (not covered by §1.56(c)) cannot file IDSs under 1.97/1.98 and may only submit patents and publications under 1.99 in published applications. For unpublished pending applications, third parties may file a protest under 1.291 prior to mailing of a notice of allowance. The Office will review and discard improper third-party IDS submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure compliance with duty of disclosure; third parties have limited mechanisms for submission and the Office will discard noncompliant third-party submissions.
